def count_strings_with_sa_lcp(sa, lcp, k):
    """Count strings realizing a prescribed suffix array and LCP array.

    A string s of length n over the integer alphabet {1, 2, ..., k} has n
    suffixes s[i:], i = 0..n-1, which are pairwise distinct. Its suffix
    array SA(s) is the permutation of 0..n-1 listing the starting positions
    of the suffixes in strictly increasing lexicographic order. Its LCP
    array LCP(s) has length n-1, where LCP(s)[i] is the length of the
    longest common prefix of s[SA(s)[i]:] and s[SA(s)[i+1]:].

    Input domain:
      sa  -- a list of ints forming a permutation of 0..n-1, 1 <= n <= 200
             (guaranteed to be a permutation);
      lcp -- a list of n-1 ints, each between 0 and n inclusive; the pair
             (sa, lcp) is NOT guaranteed to be realizable by any string;
      k   -- an int with 1 <= k <= 10**9.

    Return the exact number, as a Python int, of strings s in {1,...,k}^n
    with SA(s) == sa and LCP(s) == lcp. Return 0 if no such string exists
    (including whenever the pair (sa, lcp) is internally inconsistent, or
    the alphabet is too small). The answer may be astronomically large and
    must be exact; brute-force enumeration of the up to k**n candidate
    strings is hopeless.

    >>> count_strings_with_sa_lcp([1, 0], [1], 3)
    3
    >>> count_strings_with_sa_lcp([2, 0, 1], [1, 0], 4)
    6
    >>> count_strings_with_sa_lcp([2, 0, 1], [0, 1], 5)
    0
    >>> count_strings_with_sa_lcp([0], [], 10**9)
    1000000000
    """
